subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 9-month-old girl is evaluated for developmental regression, abdominal enlargement, and delayed myelination on MRI. Enzyme studies confirm a lysosomal storage disease with accumulation of an undegraded glycosphingolipid.
question: The progressive organ dysfunction in this infant results most directly from impaired function of which of the following processes?
explanation_correct: Lysosomal storage diseases are caused by deficiency of a lysosomal hydrolase, so its substrate cannot be degraded and accumulates within lysosomes. The engorged lysosomes and stored material interfere with normal cell function in neurons, macrophages, and other tissues.

explanation_incorrect.A: Peroxisomal beta-oxidation defects cause very long chain fatty acid accumulation and do not produce lysosomal inclusions.
explanation_incorrect.C: Proteasomal degradation removes ubiquitinated cytosolic proteins and is not the defective process here.
explanation_incorrect.D: Mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation defects cause hypoketotic hypoglycemia and myopathy.
explanation_incorrect.E: Nucleotide excision repair defects cause xeroderma pigmentosum and are unrelated to lysosomal storage.

educationalObjective: Lysosomal storage diseases arise from deficient lysosomal hydrolases, leading to intracellular accumulation of undegraded substrate.
